config.title: Generators, Iterators & Proxy

intro.title: Generators, Iterators & Proxy
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple data processing pipeline that uses JavaScript's advanced features to handle sequences of data. You'll learn the core concepts of Generators, which produce values on demand, Iterators, which define how to traverse data, and Proxy, which intercepts and customizes operations on objects. The main technologies involved are JavaScript's generator functions, the iterator protocol, and the Proxy object. By the end, you'll create a program that generates numbers, iterates through them, and logs access to an object using a proxy, all in a beginner-friendly way.
intro.usecase: Generators and iterators are essential for handling large datasets in modern web applications, such as infinite scrolling feeds in social media platforms or paginated data tables in analytics dashboards. Proxies enable reactive programming patterns by intercepting object operations, which powers frameworks like Vue.js for automatic UI updates when data changes. Developers use these patterns to create efficient data streaming in real-time dashboards, implement custom validation logic in complex forms, and build sophisticated state management systems that track user interactions across application panels and modals.

objectives: Implement a custom iterator object with a next() method that returns value-done pairs
Construct generator functions using the function* syntax and yield statements
Manipulate generator execution by calling next() and passing values back into the generator
Configure Proxy objects to intercept and customize fundamental operations on target objects
Apply Proxy handlers to control property access, assignment, and enumeration
Integrate generators with for...of loops to produce iterable sequences
Initialize Proxy with multiple traps to create reactive or validated data structures

steps.title: Create a basic iterator object
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'basicIterator' that returns an iterator object with a next() method. The next() method should return an object with 'value' and 'done' properties.
steps.hint: Remember that an iterator object must have a next() method that returns {value: any, done: boolean}.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a function that returns an iterator object with a next() method.
successCriteria: The basicIterator function exists and returns an object with a next() method that returns {value, done} objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function returns an object with a next() method that returns {value, done} objects.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Create a function named 'basicIterator' that returns an object with a next() method.

steps.title: Implement iterator for an array
steps.instruction: Create a function named arrayIterator that takes an array as a parameter and returns an iterator object with a next() method that goes through each element using an index counter.
steps.hint: The iterator object should have a next() method that returns { value: currentElement, done: false } for each element, and { value: undefined, done: true } when finished.

steps.title: Use Symbol.iterator to make object iterable
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'iterableObject' that returns an object with a Symbol.iterator method. The Symbol.iterator method should return an iterator for an array of numbers [1, 2, 3].
steps.hint: Remember that Symbol.iterator is a special property that defines how an object should be iterated. You can assign a function to it that returns an iterator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The iterableObject function should return an object that can be used in a for...of loop or with the spread operator.
successCriteria: The iterableObject function is defined and returns an object with a Symbol.iterator method that provides an iterator for [1, 2, 3].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your Symbol.iterator method returns a proper iterator object with a next() method.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined the iterableObject function correctly and that it returns an object with a Symbol.iterator property.

steps.title: Create a basic generator function
steps.instruction: Create a generator function named 'basicGenerator' using the function* syntax that yields the numbers 1, 2, and 3.
steps.hint: Generator functions are declared with function* and use the yield keyword to produce values.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a generator function that yields three sequential numbers.
successCriteria: The basicGenerator function is defined with function* syntax and yields the numbers 1, 2, and 3.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using function* and the yield keyword to produce the values.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to use function* and yield to create a generator.

steps.title: Use yield to pause execution
steps.instruction: Create a generator function named 'pauseGenerator' that yields three different string values in sequence: 'First pause', 'Second pause', and 'Third pause'.
steps.hint: Use the function keyword or arrow function syntax to define a generator function that yields three string values one after another.
steps.expectedOutcome: A generator function that yields three string values sequentially, demonstrating how yield pauses execution.
successCriteria: The pauseGenerator function yields three different string values in the correct order.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your generator yields exactly three different string values in sequence.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a generator function named 'pauseGenerator' that yields three string values.

steps.title: Pass values into generator with next()
steps.instruction: Create a new function named 'valuePassingGenerator' that demonstrates passing values into a generator using next(value). The generator should yield a value,
steps.hint: Define a generator function that yields a string, then uses a variable to capture the value passed into next(), and yields that value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A generator function that yields a prompt, receives a value via next(value), and yields it back.
successCriteria: The valuePassingGenerator function is defined, yields a string, captures the value from next(), and yields it back.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your generator yields a string first, then uses a variable to capture the value from next(), and yields that value back.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't properly demonstrate passing values into a generator. Review how to use yield to pause and next(value) to send values back into the generator.

steps.title: Create infinite sequence generator
steps.instruction: Create a generator function named infiniteSequenceGenerator that yields an infinite sequence of numbers starting from 1.
steps.hint: Use a while (true) loop inside your generator function to keep yielding numbers indefinitely.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a generator function that can produce an infinite sequence of numbers when called.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create a basic Proxy object
steps.instruction: Create a function named basicProxy that returns a Proxy object. The Proxy should wrap a target object { value: 42 } and have a handler that intercepts property access.
steps.hint: Use the Proxy constructor with two arguments: the target object and a handler object with a get trap.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that returns a Proxy object wrapping { value: 42 } with a get trap in the handler.
successCriteria: The basicProxy function is defined, uses the Proxy constructor, has a target object { value: 42 }, and includes a handler with a get method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function returns a Proxy with both a target object and a handler containing a get trap.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined a function named basicProxy that returns a Proxy object with a target and handler.

steps.title: Intercept property access with get trap
steps.instruction: In your basicProxy function, add a get trap to the handler object to intercept property reads and return a custom message.
steps.hint: Add a get method to the handler object that receives the target and property parameters, then returns a string like `Accessed property: ${property}`.
steps.expectedOutcome: The basicProxy function should return a Proxy with a get trap that intercepts property access.
successCriteria: The handler object includes a get method that returns a custom string when a property is accessed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the handler object has a get method that returns a custom message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The get trap is missing or incorrect. Add a get method to the handler object to intercept property access.

steps.title: Intercept property assignment with set trap
steps.instruction: In the basicProxy function, add a set trap to the handler object to intercept property writes. The set trap should log a message to the console when a property is set.
steps.hint: Add a set method to the handler object. The set method receives target, property, value, and receiver parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: The basicProxy function will now have a handler with a set trap that logs property assignments.
successCriteria: The handler object contains a set method that logs to console and returns true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a set method, but make sure it logs to console and returns true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The set trap is missing or incomplete. Add a set method to the handler object.

steps.title: Combine iterator and generator
steps.instruction: Create a function named combinedIteratorGenerator that returns a generator which implements the iterator protocol.
steps.hint: Define a generator function that yields values and returns an object with a next() method.
steps.expectedOutcome: A generator function that can be used as an iterator, yielding values when next() is called.
successCriteria: The combinedIteratorGenerator function is defined and returns a generator that implements the iterator protocol.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is a generator (uses function* syntax) and yields values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a generator function named combinedIteratorGenerator that yields values.

steps.title: Create Proxy with generator for lazy evaluation
steps.instruction: Create a function named lazyProxy that returns a Proxy object with a get trap that uses a generator to lazily evaluate properties.
steps.hint: Define a generator inside the get trap that yields values based on the property name being accessed.
steps.expectedOutcome: A lazyProxy function that returns a Proxy with a get trap using a generator for lazy property evaluation.
successCriteria: The lazyProxy function exists, returns a Proxy, and has a get trap that uses a generator to lazily evaluate accessed properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your lazyProxy function returns a Proxy with a get trap that contains a generator function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a function named lazyProxy that returns a Proxy with a get trap using a generator.
